canonical_plan.active_item: 77.44.7.D / D-06; EDT-039 page interaction timer lifecycle

finding: A delayed page action remained armed after its authored trigger was removed from a still-connected page root. If a dynamic subtree removed the trigger before its timer fired, the callback could still change another element on the page.

details: The timer callback now runs only while the page root is connected, its original trigger remains contained by that root, and the document is visible. The timer still removes its pending entry when it fires.

Added focused unit and real-Chromium lifecycle regressions: a detached authored trigger cannot change the target; an attached trigger still applies the timer action. A full-page Chromium lifecycle regression removes a published trigger while preserving the page and checks that the destination tabs remain unchanged.
Refreshed the Editor entry and public renderer cache tokens and updated the cache-bust contract test. Save continues to modify only the draft; Publish remains an explicit separate action.
